A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, equations, figures and tables were readable and matched across versions. V1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–D. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments measuring Hits@k, response types and SkipUnsure accuracy across LLaMA/Qwen models and the DBPedia, IMDB and GoodReads datasets.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds Mistral evaluations and further model-by-dataset Hits@k results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: SkipUnsure becomes 'Decoding Without Unsure Tokens,' but the procedure remains the same: filter uninformative tokens, select the highest-probability remaining candidate, append it to the prompt and regenerate. Equation 2 and the substantive algorithm steps are unchanged; its analytical purpose is reframed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate factual QA on DBPedia, IMDB and GoodReads using head, torso and tail subsets. Appendix A newly documents dataset snapshots and provenance without establishing different data coverage. No new task or input scenario is demonstrated.

E2.justification: The decoding comparison remains unfiltered greedy decoding versus the same token-filtering procedure. Mistral is an additional backbone evaluated with both procedures, rather than a new competing decoding method. No distinct comparator algorithm is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 adds Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 as an evaluated model configuration. The stated popularity splits, three-character matching criterion and temperature-zero greedy decoding remain unchanged. Dataset dates and the exact prompt are newly disclosed details, not established changes to existing settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D substantially broadens k-sensitivity evidence: v1 illustrates k dependence with LLaMA3-8B plots, whereas v2 reports k=5, 10 and 50 across all nine models, three datasets and popularity subsets. Existing response-type analyses and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Discussion of 'unsure' responses concerns model behavior, not a new statistical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds Mistral results and extensive lower-k results in Tables 3–5. Figure 4 also changes existing reported values: DBPedia-head Hits@1 changes from 17.2 to 18.9, and Hits@5 from 57.9 to 48.3, under the retained LLaMA3-8B label. Existing LLaMA/Qwen entries in Table 1 and the filtering comparison tables are retained.

T1.justification: The Hits@k definition in Equation 1 and filtered-token selection in Equation 2 remain mathematically equivalent. No theorem, proof, derivation or formal assumption is added. The new metric-validity discussion is an empirical interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the prominent contribution of a practical SkipUnsure accuracy-improvement method with an investigation of how 'unsure'-permitting prompts mask correct knowledge. The storage–expression gap and Hits@k contributions remain, but the final central contribution changes substantially.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly restricts filtering to an analytical probe, replacing v1's emphasis on easy deployment. It attributes answer suppression to conservative decoding or confidence calibration and introduces a defense of Hits@k as genuine knowledge rather than token co-occurrence. These substantially revise the interpretation and applicability of retained experiments.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C disclose dataset snapshot dates, GoodReads provenance and the exact two-example QA prompt. A new reproducibility statement promises code and instructions upon publication; it does not establish present availability. These improve documentation without providing a complete implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wan and McAuley (2018) as the GoodReads data source. The related-work survey otherwise retains the same works and substantive descriptions, while the introduction drops SkipUnsure's comparative deployment advantages.

P1.justification: The abstract, closing introduction, contribution list, Section 5 and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the analytical framing. V2 also adds ethics and reproducibility statements and Appendices A–D. These are substantial narrative and structural changes despite much retained text.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column format with a predominantly single-column layout, rearranges multipanel Figures 2, 3 and 7, and redesigns Figure 6. The former Tables 2–3 become a combined Table 2 with revised headings and caption; three appendix tables and a boxed prompt are added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through the dataset details and exact prompt, broadens sensitivity evidence, and appropriately limits deployment claims. However, its new metric-validity and reliability assertions lack corresponding validation, and retained accuracy results are ambiguously relabeled 'recovery rates.' Sections 1 and 2.3 still quote 17.2% and 57.9%, although revised Figure 4 shows 18.9% and 48.3%. These benefits and central reporting problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
